#3985. GTA 6 Players Warned To Turn Off Auto-Uploads Or Risk Getting Banned On Xbox

Xbox is handing out bans to GTA 6 players for uploading game captures that 'accidentally' breach its family and online safety guidelines.

On by default, game captures automatically uploaded to Xbox Live servers are scanned for offensive imagery, including hate speech, drugs misuse, excessive violence, as well as nudity and sexual content.

According to some Reddit sleuthing, GTA 6 players are being banned for uploading content captured on the beach in Leonida amongst other activities. The original poster claimed to have captured "zero nudity-just standard Vice City beach/coastal gameplay with NPCs in swimsuits/bikinis" before getting slapped with a ToS violation.

If you think about it, it would be odd to walk around a beach with a video camera filming the locals, but it's a bit silly to see Xbox players getting 2-day bans. The rulings appear to be automated and unappealable too.

It's not clear if sexual content or nudity is the cause for the violation, but it's worth noting GTA 6 does contain full-frontal nudity. We'd recommend not spamming the capture button during those sequences. Xbox doesn't like that sort of thirsty behaviour.

If you're worried about getting a 2-day ban in the height of GTA 6 fever, then perhaps you could consider turning off automatic uploads in your Xbox settings. Here's a quick guide on how to do this:

#3983. Conan: The Black Pyramid shoves the titular barbarian into a very Hades-inspired action roguelite with the addition of a few other familiar heroes

I feel like one thing I only sort of miss from my youth, viewed through the lenses of those rose tinted goggles, is the established intellectual property game that just copies the formula of another, successful game. Obviously there are plenty of genres that are trendy to imitate, but how often do you see something that's just sort of "thing you know slapped on top of game you know?" Perhaps that's a tad mean, but I do genuinely have a fondness for such games, so I'm quite pleased by the announcement of Conan: The Black Pyramid, an action roguelite RPG that so clearly went to Supergiant Games' School of Hades you have to admire the boldness just a little bit.

Conan: The Black Pyramid puts you in the hotseat as the titular barbarian, of course, but also as other characters from the series like Solomon Kane, Dark Agnes, and apparently, more! So, immediately, a notable enough difference from Hades, and one that seems like a neat take. As one of them you then "Descend into eldritch chambers of the Black Pyramid, a mysterious and dangerous place that defies the logic of space and time. Confront the shadows of the champions themselves and piece together the dark secrets of their past."

Where it is similar to Hades lies in the fact that the titular triangle changes in form each time you go in it, and of course there are different abilities and buffs to pick up along the way to aid you in your quest. Each character has their own combination of weapons and abilities, so it does sound like you can mix it up quite nicely. There is, also, 2-player online co-op (sorry to the couch lovers, I suppose), adding to the ways it differs and making it a tad more friendly for those that have exactly one friend who also loves Conan.

Overall, seems like a fresh enough take on Hades while still trying to find some amount of its own identity. And hey, Hades is great, so I'm never upset about having a little bit more of that kind of game. No release date attached to Conan: The Black Pyramid just yet, but it is planned to arrive sometime in 2027. You can check it out on Steam here.

#3982. Ubisoft is reportedly making a new Rainbow Six Vegas game, nearly two decades after Vegas 2

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a new Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three new projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

It’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Rainbow Six Vegas launched in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

#3981. Warhammer 40,000: Darktide's next class is the Sisters Novitiate, a group who love staking and burning people for the God-Emperor, and its out next month

Look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a new Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!

According to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game. "Unlike other classes, the Sisters Novitiate are able to choose from six divine and devastating Acts of Faith, as opposed to blitz and combat abilities," the post explains. "Their abilities draw upon reserves of Faith, allowing them to unleash brutal Neural Whip attacks to the inspiring Icon of Purity and protective prayers. Faith can take many forms for the Sisters Novitiate, each channeling the Emperor's divine will and bringing his wrath upon his enemies."

You build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use. Any two Acts of Faith can be equipped at a time, allowing players to choose how their Novitiate will unleash righteous fury on the battlefield." I mentioned crossbows, right? Well, I stand lore corrected, as what they technically have is the Condemnor Stakethrower, which "pins what remains of their enemies to the walls." They do also have access to a flamethrower, a big ole mace, your classic sword and shield, and whatever the hell a "Penitent Eviscerator."

This DLC class also comes the same day as a free update, which will introduce the Metlagun, equipable by the Sisters Novitiate as well as the Veteran. Apparently there'll be more information on the free update soon. Oh, and the release date! It's December 7th, so a little under a month away. I'm sure you can (Dark)tide over the next few weeks by rewatching the gnarly reveal trailer.

#3980. Report: Xbox's New Zealand Trick Has Been Used By Crazy Numbers Of People This Week

Ahead of the launch of GTA 6, there was a whole lot of talk online about the Xbox "New Zealand trick" and how people could get early access to the game by switching their regions to New Zealand on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

We mentioned in various articles how it was a risky practice (against Xbox's ToCs), but one that had never traditionally resulted in any widespread bans, and it doesn't seem like either Xbox or Rockstar took any action at first glance.

As it turns out, a lot of people decided to give it a go for the new Grand Theft Auto.

This is according to the folks at Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business), who report that over 2.1 million people played GTA 6 in the US and the UK before it was officially released.

As you can see from the graph above, it seems the vast majority of those were based in the United States, followed by the UK, Canada, Brazil and Mexico. Only around 100,000 people tried the trick on PS5 in the U.S. (where it's harder to implement and requires a separate account), whereas 1.5 million of them ended up using it on Xbox.

Ultimately, the existence of the New Zealand trick probably led to a bunch of increased sales for Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it also poses the question of whether Xbox might be forced to put a stop to it on Project Helix and beyond. As much it's a beloved feature, it's also being used in a way that wasn't originally intended.

Let's see what happens in the future, but for now, it's clearly made a lot of people happy this week!

#3979. GTA 6 Censorship in Japan Sees Characters Shower in Underwear, as Sex and Violence Are Toned Down

GTA 6 has been censored to a fairly large extent in Japan, where the country's strict ratings system often sees nudity, sexual content, and graphic violence be toned down or removed entirely in video games.

To be clear, GTA 6 has been given Japan's highest 18+ age rating — but it's still had to make changes in order to ensure its release in the region.

For starters, Rockstar's latest is packed with full-on nudity — to a degree never before seen in a mainstream release — but in Japan, it's apparently impossible to remove the underwear of main characters Jason and Lucia, even when they're taking a shower.

The same is true of NPCs — everyone's always wearing at least one layer to cover up their privates.

Needless to say, the game's numerous sex scenes have also been censored. Again, it's a case of keeping clothes on — but some specific scenes have actually been cut completely.

Violence is next on the list. GTA 6 obviously features a lot of bloodshed but it's also rather gory, with accurate depictions of dismemberment and lethal physical trauma. It can all come across as particularly gruesome given how realistic the game looks.

In Japan, it seems as though most of this stuff is scaled back. There's less blood spray in general, and spilled blood doesn't stay in place very long.

It's a little unclear just how far this censorship of violence goes, but it's not uncommon for Japan to remove things like dismemberment — especially if a game's got a grounded setting.

For what it's worth, GTA 6 does have several settings that let you change the amount of blood and gore that's on display. I assume that in Japan, these settings are applied at a censored standard by default.

Interestingly, though, drug use seemingly hasn't been touched. Japan's got very strict anti-drug laws, but illegal goods are still totally usable in GTA 6.

Did you see this censorship coming? Try not to go on a blood-soaked rampage in the comments section below.

#3978. The latest GTA 6 leak comes in the form of a 34-song tracklist for GTA 6: The Album, featuring Dua Lipa, Lana Del Rey, Rina Sawayama, and more

We are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a new video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - showed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

Thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:

You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

#3977. Fatal Fury: City Of The Wolves Adds Laocorn From The Motion Picture

Reminder: The Fatal Fury movie antagonist is now available

Update [Sun 22nd Nov 2026, 4am]: Here's your reminder that Laocorn is now available in Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves on the Switch 2 and other platforms. He rolls out alongside the latest game update (Version 3.4.1).

"From Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture, Laocorn Gaudeamus joins the battle! Discover more about the sinister movie villain who once pushed Terry to his limits in his new Arcade and EOST stories! Now, players can finally wield the awesome power of Mars themselves, only in FATAL FURY: City of the Wolves!"

You can also check out the animated trailer for the relase of this character in the video above. Here's some backstory:

"Still haunted by Sulia's death, Terry finds himself confronted by the ghosts of his past when the Triumvirate suddenly returns. Drawn into a new battle over the power residing within the Armor of Mars, Terry and his companions must fight once again."

Original Story: [Sun 15th Nov, 2026 08:30 GMT]:

SNK's expansion of the Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves roster will continue with the release of Laocorn next week on 19th November 2026.

This character, who was the primary antagonist in the 1994 anime movie Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture, is part of the game's paid Season 3 DLC line up, and is voiced by Branden Loera.

"Primary antagonist in the 1994 anime film Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture. Laocorn and his twin sister Sulia are direct descendants of Gaudeamus, a mighty warrior from antiquity. With his ever-loyal Triumvirate in tow, he relentlessly pursues the legendary Armor of Mars—intent on transcending humanity and ascending to godhood.

"When he discovers the armor's final piece is part of the prize for the KOF tournament, he enters the competition himself. But will claiming the armor bring him the power he craves—or a fate beyond his control?"

You can check out the trailer above (note: the YouTube video uses auto-dubbing, which does not reflect the voice acting in the game). SNK has also released a "digest movie" of the motion picture to help set the scene:

"Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture (1994) Determined to stop her brother, Laocorn Gaudeamus, from completing the forbidden Armor of Mars, Sulia Gaudeamus ventures alone to South Town in search of Terry Bogard, the hero she hopes can thwart Laocorn's dark ambitions."

Laocorn joins Rick Strowd, Duck King, Kim Kaphwan and Manjiro Sano & Ken Ryuguji as part of Season 3. In December, SNK is also teaming up with Tekken 8, which will see the arrival of Reina in the game. If you haven't already played City of the Wolves on Switch 2, there's a demo you can check out on the eShop.

#3976. Barbie Rewind, out now, invites you to take a trip down memory lane with a whole bunch of life in plastic classics, and one game that was previously unreleased

Is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

The latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's important because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

Beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history."

Perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

#3975. GTA 6's Mandy 'Is a Lot of Fun' Says Real-Life Actress as PS5 Players Are Smitten

I knew when I was reviewing GTA 6 that bunny boiler Mandy was going to take social media by storm, and it was quite fun watching the web react to Chapter 1’s ‘Pipeworks’ mission as the game launched overnight.

Now it’s being played by millions, actress Lexie Shoaibi has revealed she stars as the character, who not-so subtly throws herself at Jason during a very early story mission.

I actually think this is one example of the game’s slightly more mature writing. Wait, don’t roll your eyes – just hear me out, okay?

While this whole quest is played more for laughs, it’s there to establish the strength of Jason and Lucia’s relationship, as Jason shows no signs of being tempted by Mandy’s advances.

“She’s a lot of fun,” Shoaibi said, after confirming she did voice acting and motion capture for the character. At the time of writing, her post on Instagram has received over 90k likes.

But the response on social media would suggest gamers think she’s more than a “lot of fun”.

One post by Complex, featuring a few images and the caption ‘Mandy from GTA 6’, attracted 37 million views in just a few hours. Pertinently, it’s been bookmarked 54k times.

I don’t want to analyse this character too deeply, but I think it’s the moment I realised Rockstar has really pushed the boat out here.

The sheer variety of body types, and the detail invested into them, is unprecedented really. Mandy is just one of many similarly realistic NPCs in the game.

And while the character is almost certainly a psychopath, it’s been amusing to see her go viral overnight.

#3974. Blade Runner 2099 bosses hint at a possible "triple-A" Blade Runner game in the future - just don't expect it any time soon

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

#3972. Cover your robot body in magical fungus aplenty and galavant across a mystical, Soulslike world in MycoRelic, now out in 1.0

Robot, robot, robot, robot, mushroom! Mushroom!

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

MycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite quickly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

For starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

#3971. Katsuhiro Harada Reveals The Pokémon He Wanted To Add To Pokken Tournament

Famous Japanese game director and producer Katsuhiro Harada, known for the Bandai Namco series Tekken, has revealed a Pokémon he wanted to add to the Pokémon fighting game Pokken Tournament but it didn't make the cut.

Harada, who worked as a producer on both versions of the game, wanted the fighting / dark-type Pokémon 'Pangoro' from Generation VI. As for why he wanted to include it, Harada thought it had a "really cool" design and almost looked like it was wearing a traditional Japanese school uniform.

There were many discussions before finalising the roster, and a lot of it came down to the gameplay and systems in place, along with The Pokémon Company's own requests. Here's what Harada had to say about this (via EventHubs):

Harada: "We had thorough discussions before finalizing the roster. There were Pokémon that the development team wanted to include from a gameplay and systems perspective, and of course, The Pokémon Company also had its own requests for which Pokémon they wanted to see in the game."

After the release of Pokken Tournament DX for Switch, the final roster included the following Pokémon (this included some Switch-exclusive and DLC Pokémon).

As you can see, the final roster is an interesting mix. Harada, who is now the CEO and game director of SNK's VS Studio, added how he was just personally happy at the time to see the lineup include Pikachu and Gengar.

#3970. Treyarch lays off lead Call of Duty writer and Zombies veteran after "approximately 20 years" of service

"Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the company and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years."

On Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox announced earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

Houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

If you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he announced the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

"Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material."

"You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," says ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...]."

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

#3969. Slay the Spire 2's "biggest" beta patch yet adds its first new early access and foolish character, two game modes, and more tweaks than you can shake a stick at

Hark! A new Slay the Spire 2 patch is here! Or, well, it is if you're someone who's trying out the beta branches of the game. If you're not, it might be worth trying out, as Mega Crit say this is their biggest patch for the game so far, with "some really impactful bits of content that will require lots of testing before they reach the main branch."

First up, a new character: The Fool! "Wah!! The first new character for Early Access arrives!" a Steam blog post explains. "A silly musician who wields a bow! How can such a whimsical creature survive within the Spire? Why, that's up to you! We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch. Even more importantly, be sure to have fun figuring out all the strategies and story of this gently bard. It would be foolish not to!" The post doesn't go into much detail as to what the new character can actually do, so, you'll have to discover that one for yourself!

There are also two new game modes to try out with this beta update. The first is Blitz, a "condensed and chaotic deckbuilding-focused mode." Here, the "Merchant's wares feel a bit off, the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters." You'll also find it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across every character, and you can unlock it by completing an Ascension run on any difficulty. The second mode is Dread, which as the name implies, is a "brutal" difficulty mode that you can only play if you've reached Ascension 10 on every character, including The Fool. "All ascension modifiers are enabled. Bosses are stronger and buff all enemies in their Act. Curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire. Death is expected."

You can expect a bunch of new balance tweaks and changes too. For starters, you'll find that rest sites can now appear a floor earlier every act. New events have been added to Underdocks and Act 2 and 3 too. Some nice quality of life alterations have been made, like how the character select screen for standard runs will start on whatever character you played as last, and controller navigation at the Merchant has been improved too. You can read all about the rest of the many changes right here.

#3968. Wolverine PS5's Sales Absolutely Plunged in October

Marvel’s Wolverine may have started strong in September’s Circana sales report, but it plunged in October.

Sony’s big PS5 exclusive for 2026, which attracted reasonable if utterly unremarkable reviews, ranked 14th in the latest US best-sellers list – dropping dramatically from first position the month of its release.

The game is now 15th overall for 2026 as a whole, down from 11th position in September. It’ll continue to fall with juggernauts like GTA 6 now officially out.

Couple other notes: Marvel's Wolverine dropped from 1st in Sept to 14th in Oct, ranks in top 15 YTD. On the YTD charts, less than $10M separates 8th place from 13th - it's a tight cluster.

The exclusive’s lore accurate lack of legs can likely be attributed to the game’s worse than expected reviews.

While it’s not universally disliked – we awarded it an 8/10, after all – fans understandably expect better from dev Insomniac.

Sony’s running discounts on the game during Black Friday to try and stimulate some enthusiasm around it, and I suspect this may be one of those titles that ends up in a lot of hardware bundles in the future.

To be fair, the platform holder seemed relatively satisfied with the title’s 2.4 million sales during its recent financial report.

I suppose it’s possible the launch numbers really did meet its expectations, but it may now be disappointed with the title’s long-term momentum – or lack thereof.

We’ll probably have to wait until its next investor update before we get more information.

There’s certainly some truth in that, and it’s always been the common wisdom. But I think the AAA market is a bit more complex now. Many of these big AAA games also get really long tail sales, they rely of that for making a lot of extra profit and getting people into the IP later.

Look at GoW: Ragnarok reportedly selling 20+ million units, yet only around 5 million were in the first week. Similar for Spider-man, Horizon, TLOU, GT7 and other big IP that keep selling long after release, they only hit those huge milestones from long tail sales. There was even an article on Bloodborne selling another 250k copies last year.

Of course not all sales are equal, financially day 1 sales will be at full price where as long tail sales will often be at a discount. And month 1 sales may also be used to judge a games success and make decisions for the studio going forward, they are still vital but don’t tell the whole story.

#3967. Cyberpunk 2077 mod Torrent adds 3D rain, lightning storms, and tyre spray to Night City

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

As spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

The rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

#3966. HDR Expert Shares Their Three Recommended Display Settings For GTA 6

The good (and hilarious) folks over at HDTVTest have been looking at the HDR Calibration settings for GTA 6 on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and they've discovered that the tool is actually slightly broken as things stand.

Some of the specifics go over my head a little bit to be honest, but in a nutshell, the figures that are displayed on the calibration tool don't fully translate into the game itself, leading to a potentially inoptimal picture.

As a result, they've published a new nine-minute video (which you can see up above) to explain the issues.

"The HDR calibration screen in GTA 6 can be misleading, because Rockstar's Max Brightness, Paper White and Black Levels settings interact in unexpected ways. To be clear, GTA VI's HDR rendering isn't broken… it's the calibration procedure that can give misleading results."

The video goes step-by-step on how they analysed the issues and tried to figure out the best possible HDR settings for GTA 6, and while their tests aren't fully concluded yet (there's another video to come in the future where they try multiple consumer displays), they've shared their initial best settings for displays capable of 1,000 nits or brighter.

Here are those three settings, but again, keep in mind that your TV must be capable of 1,000 nits of brightness or more, and that certain smart TV features or special HDR settings on your TV itself may interfere with the results.

If your display isn't capable of 1,000 nits, do a bit of Googling to try and find out the specifics for your TV/monitor, and then times that figure by two in-game. So, if you're working with a maximum of 600 nits, set the figure as 1,200.

I have to be honest and say I'm not seeing a lot of difference here, but I've also got an old TV with a max brightness of just over 600 nits, not to mention I'm using a few image-altering features that may be playing havoc with the settings. It's also noted in the video that this is generally based on playing in the dark, rather than in a brightly-lit room.

Have a play for yourself and see what you think - there's clearly a lot of people who are very thankful for these settings on YouTube and beyond, so we wanted to at least make you aware of them. The reality is that you may need to still do a bit of tweaking to find the perfect sweet spot for your setup though.

#3965. Poll: Which Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga Box Art Is The Best?

Ahoy folks, and welcome to another edition of Box Art Brawl!

Looking back on last week, we checked out Dr. Mario & Puzzle League for the GBA to celebrate its recent addition to the NSO library. Neither design in this instance was particularly enthralling, and this is perhaps evident in the final result. Japan just about managed to claim a win with 51% of the vote, with North America / Europe making up the remaining 49%. Oof, so close!

We're sticking with the GBA this week to peruse the box art designs for Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga. Released in 2003, this was the debut title in the spin-off RPG series, and arguably still its best. It was remade for the 3DS (and we did a Box Art Brawl for that one, too), but man, there's something about those GBA visuals that just make it, y'know?

North America and Europe share the same design for this one, so they'll be teaming up against Japan. Let's do this!

#3964. Wolfenstein 3 and new id Software game confirmed, as Xbox boss somehow unrelatedly shouts about one person soon wielding "capabilities that once required entire nations"

Asha Sharma had a normal one as Xbox turned 25

Xbox have confirmed that Wolfenstein 3 is indeed in production at Indiana Jones and the Great Circle devs MachineGames and that Doom makers id Software have started work on their next game after losing a bunch of staff to the mass layoffs across Microsoft's gaming division this year.

"A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations," isn't part of the marketing spiel for either of those games. Instead, it's something Xbox CEO Asha Shama has bellowed amid a rant outlining how she sees the company's future.

The Wolfenstein and id confirmations came as Xbox had a bit of a social media party to commemorate their 25th birthday. Sharma, ever keen to be seen right next to any positive news coming out of the company, confirmed Wolfenstein 3 is in production by posting a photo showing a few lines from its script. Around the same time, she shouted out Doom: The Dark Ages Revelations' incoming Slaughter Mode, adding that "the team is already working on its next game".

The official id Software account responded to note that this next game is being made by their "teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin", and that "it'll be some time before [they're] ready to share more".

We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on.

Alongside hollering about these couple of games, Sharma put out a 25th anniversary statement which for the most part does the sort of bigging up of Xbox's past you'd expect. Good times were had, we blazed a trail and made lots of money, etcetera. The final section saw the exec attempt to look forward to the next 25 years for Xbox.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically," she wrote. "As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this.

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today's games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

That certainly sounds a lot like the sales pitch the biggest proponents of generative AI keep wheeling out, while avoiding saying generative AI out loud in the hopes of making it more palatable to folks who might not make the connection. I'm waiting for Sharma to put out another post revealing that she accidentally mixed another section of the Wolfenstein script into her celebratory musings, but I'm not holding my breath.

Xbox parent company Microsoft are still currently subject to a BDS movement boycott over their reported ties to the Israeli military.

#3963. Police arrest suspect after drive-by shooting at office campus housing Xbox studio inXile

Police are still investigating the motive.

Police have arrested a suspect after a drive-by shooting at an office campus in Tustin, California, which is home to Xbox-owned studio inXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

"Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Police have not given a motive, and the suspect has not been named.

InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is currently working on Clockwork Revolution.

#3962. Guide: GTA 6: Radio Songs - All Music, Radio Stations, & Artists

As with the previous games in the series, GTA 6 has a staggering amount of both licensed and original music. There's so much to listen to, whether it's selected tracks during key story moments or you're just driving around with the radio on. In this GTA 6 guide, we're going to tell you everything you need to know about GTA 6's music.

On this page: All Radio Songs and Artists in GTA 6

Below is a list of every radio song in the game, divided by where and how they appear throughout GTA 6.

French electronic duo Justice has composed and produced the original score for GTA 6, providing music that soundtracks the entire experience. Here's the track list:

GTA 6: The Album is a selection of 34 original tracks produced just for GTA 6. Many of these also play on certain radio stations, listed below. Here's the album's track list:

As is tradition in the GTA series, GTA 6 features many radio stations you can listen to while going about your business in Leonida. Here, we list each station, along with all the songs they play. Songs that are totally new for the game are highlighted in bold.

As well as the radio stations, GTA 6 includes a number of original podcast series to enjoy. Each one features multiple episodes to listen to, unlocking as you progress. Here they all are:

The radio and podcasts can be listened to in a number of ways in GTA 6.

The most obvious way is while driving. In any vehicle, if the radio isn't on already, hold Left and turn it on with Cross/X. You can scroll through stations with L1 and R1:

To access podcasts, move the right stick down:

Outside of vehicles, you can find radios dotted around the environment; you can toggle them on with Left and choose a station (you cannot listen to podcasts on a radio):

Another option is to use headphones or earbuds.

Electronics stores sell over-ear headphones and earbuds, which allow you to listen to radio stations and podcasts while you're on foot.

To find an electronics store, open the map with Touch Pad, then use the directional buttons to reach Style, then Electronics. Nearby shops will populate the list, and you can set a waypoint from there:

Once you've bought a pair, equip them by holding L1, pressing R1 to access your items, then highlighting Headgear and pressing Cross/X as shown:

Now, you will be able to select radio stations and podcasts just like when you're driving.

GTA 6 features numerous musical artists and other celebrities, making cameo appearances in the game. Here they all are:

That's it for our guide to the radio songs in GTA 6. What are your favourite tunes to listen to in the game? Tell us in the comments section below, and be sure to check out our GTA 6 guide for much more.

#3961. Talking Point: How Often Are You Willing To Play Games At 30FPS?

While GTA 6 has been receiving unbelievable praise and is technically considered one of the best video games of all time according to Metacritic, that certainly doesn't mean it's immune to criticism.

One of the big talking points both before and after launch has been that it's a 30FPS experience across all Xbox and PlayStation consoles, and if you're going from 60FPS back to 30FPS, there's definitely an adjustment period. Some people are absolutely fine with that, while others are finding it extremely difficult to go back.

For what it's worth, our friends at Digital Foundry have been analysing this in depth today:

Feature Why Isn't Grand Theft Auto 6 60fps?

Digital FoundryAnd could frame generation be the solution?

Rockstar Games has already confirmed recently that even the PS5 Pro doesn't come close to running GTA 6 at 60FPS due to the system's processor not being powerful enough, so we might be forced to wait until the next generation of consoles (and PC) before the game will become playable at 60 frames per-second.

"The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.”

With all of this in mind, we're interested to hear what you think about playing games at 30FPS on Xbox, PlayStation or anywhere else. It's becoming much more common that 60FPS is the default these days, but there are still some phenomenal 30FPS-only experiences out there, and it's a shame to think people are missing out on them.

I personally much prefer playing at 60FPS if I can, and there are certain games I will avoid at 30FPS until they get a patch down the line (like Mafia: Definitive Edition), but when it comes to industry-defining masterpieces like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Grand Theft Auto VI, the last thing I'd want is for them to scale back the detail in order to squeeze in a 60FPS mode.

Here's how Grand Theft Auto 6 looks across both Xbox consoles

News Three Big Takeaways From Digital Foundry's GTA 6 Analysis For Xbox Series X|S

So, what do you think? Tell us in the poll above and in the comments section below.

Fraser is the News Editor at Pure Xbox, where he spends his time reporting on the biggest stories in the world of Xbox and beyond.

360–500 Hz → diminishing returns, but some users still perceive differences in latency and motion clarity

#3960. Horu is a sci-fi 4X RTS inspired by Star Wars: Empire at War in which spaceships are spellcasters who can summon black holes

Clicking a random link this morning, I was dazzled by the glare of a thousand laser batteries firing simultaneously. My ears trembled beneath the trundle of a million caterpillar tracks. Balls of ice, bolts of lightning, shipments of rare alloys, and cascades of drop pods went screaming down my nerves and detonated in my frontal cortex, painting starlanes across the inside of my skull. "Oh god, they've finally found us!" I yelled, hiding beneath my desk. "I for one welcome our new galactic overlords!"

But then I realised that I wasn't looking at a live newsfeed, but merely the Steam page for Horu, a real-time 4X strategy game in which you can "command hundreds of thousands of units across land and space", in the summary of developer David "GlassBeaver" Nadaski. There's also a magic system, this being "the spice that makes your enemy's defeat bitter", which is a very genteel way to characterise glaciating a tank formation or conjuring a miniature blackhole.

In development for years, and running on a custom C++ engine, Horu is inspired by 2006 hybrid RTS Star Wars: Empire at War - good, not great, in the words of turncoat jankonaut Graham, and the subject of many mods. Horu's way of bettering Empire at War is seemingly to add a shedload more of everything. You can engage in a fleet battle that looks like two migrating ant hives colliding, even as a frankly unnecessary quantity of cyborgs pour over the forgeworld beneath and get their shit kicked in by some tornado-summoning sorcerers.

Offensives appear to work like this: any drop ships that push through the fleet battle add meat to the ground invasion, with the option of deploying wormholes to sneak your troops behind the defending armada. On the ground, you're basically out to capture control points. You're allegedly spared from "continuous babysitting" by semi-autonomous squadron commanders and an orders system that lets you queue up objectives, before units engage in battle.

You can still give individual orders to units, but that seems like a recipe for acute wrist injury. There's also a boarding action mechanic whereby your hijackers move through vessels room by room. Again, I struggle to understand how you'll have time and dexterity to oversee such skulduggery when there are a bajillion particle cannons going off all at once.

Outside of combat, there are planets to develop, shipyards to build, spy networks to groom, research trees to water, and stock markets to manipulate. It all looks like business as usual for an imperial 4X. Honestly, I can imagine the maximalist warfaring being a hot mess, and then there's the fact that the dev is running a Kickstarter "to fund the remaining assets needed for a playable build: more spaceships, more units, more animations, more sounds, more music, and everything in between." I've been burned by Kickstarter overpromising before. Still, I can only admire the vindictive intellect that would have me play a little game of FTL inside what looks like one of the larger PvP scraps from Eve Online.

You can read more on Steam. Release date there is currently none. For an equally populous strategy experience that's closer in style to Supreme Commander, check out Sanctuary: Shattered Space.

#3959. EA hires another former Call of Duty boss to take the lead on all Battlefield Studios' projects

EA has made some notable leadership changes within its studios group, and in who oversees the Battlefield franchise. Byron Beede, previously Battlefield's general manager, has been promoted to group general manager.

Beede announced the change on LinkedIn, saying that he now oversees EA's shooter and action-RPG portfolio, seemingly occupying the role of the late Vince Zampella.

In this stead, EA appointed Sam Cooper as Battlefield's new boss. Cooper, who also revealed his new job title on LinkedIn, previously had a stint at EA Sports, but he's mostly known for his work at Activision, where he spent the last five-ish years as Call of Duty's global product management and head of live service.

While this might seem like fairly unremarkable corporate news - executives move between rival companies all the time, after all - it reinforces a narrative that EA continues to keenly replicate Activision's Call of Duty model.

That particular push is years-old now, and it kicked off in 2021 when EA hired Byron Beede, former boss of all of Call of Duty at Activision, to lead the next evolution of Battlefield. So far, that decision has given us the very successful Battlefield 6 and its free-to-play, COD: Warzone-like battle royale mode Redsec.

To facilitate that, EA rearranged several of its studios to serve under one banner dubbed Battlefield Studios, replicating Activision's model of locking several teams around the world into developing and supporting a single game / franchise. Ripple Effect, Motive, the iconic Criterion and, of course, series creator DICE are all the Battlefield franchise's lead and support studios.

Many players argue - and I would agree - that Battlefield and Call of Duty games are more alike today than they've ever been. The user interface, the emphasis on limited-time events, the garish store cosmetics, the COD-like battle pass system - complete with a more expensive option, are all signs of that transition. And that is to say nothing of controversial changes to longstanding Battlefield tenets, such as the class system, intended to make Battlefield 6 appeal to a wider audience.

The effects of that leadership change likely won't materialise until the next Battlefield title, but it's a curious one to keep in mind as EA leans even harder into its biggest franchises following its $55bn private equity and Saudi Arabia's PIF-funded buyout.

#3958. Mailbox: Ocarina Intruders, Pikmin Day, Too Many Humans - Nintendo Life Letters

Hello, you. Yes, you. It's just us here today - everyone else is busy in Hyrule or Leonida right now.

In fact, it's been like that for most of the month, it seems, as the Nintendo Life Mailbox is looking pretty empty! So, it'll be a nice quick one this month. We'll have you back with your preferred ride — equine or automotive — in a jiffy.

Got something you want to get off your chest? Remember, we're ready and waiting to read about your game-related ponderings as we head into the holidays. Each month we’ll highlight a Star Letter, the writer of which will receive a month’s subscription to our ad-free Supporter scheme. Check out the submission guidelines at the bottom of this page.

So, let's slice open our correspondence...

I've been inspired to share in this letter about my first encounter with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time following the feature you ran on this very topic, because it's a touching, unique story.

I was about 11 years old in 1998 and had been avidly following OoT in the magazines, absorbing every screenshot and article about this sword and shield weilding greened tuniced hero.

Bizarrely I'd never played a Zelda game before but something about it looked magical and exciting. So I did what any 11 year old would do. I asked for the game for Christmas.

So, Christmas morning arrives and I excitedly tumble down the stairs to the presents under the tree. I open them all but.... There's a pang of absence. No Zelda game. Where is it I exclaim!? And my mum sheepishly informs me that it didn't arrive in time for Christmas.

I cry. Real tears. I'm distraught. Inconsolable. For months I've waited for this amazing looking game and I can't play it.

What happened next is... I think... wonderful parenting.

While I was busy in my bedroom creating my own water temple with more tears than a kingdom (see what I did there?), my mum phones every parent of my school friends she knows until she finds someone with a copy of Zelda. And eventually, she does. She creeps up to knock on my door and says "Hey, Listen! I'll take you to your friends place, he has a copy"

And so, my tears stop and off I go to watch my pal play the game and suddenly a terrible Christmas becomes a brilliant one. The game is everything I imagine it to be and more and my mate and I spend hours solving Deku Tree puzzles and gasping at Hyrule Field's majesty.

So as we all enjoy the remake of Ocarina of Time decades later, I just have one thing to say: Thanks mum. You understood the stakes and you cared enough to help me get my Zelda fix that fateful Christmas of 1998.

And ever since that day, my life has been met with the least terrible of fates: I became a huge fan of Zelda and have bought every single one since on day one - no more painful Christmas mornings! YoshiTails

That is some above-and-beyond parenting, Mrs YoshiTails! We salute you.

I'm imagining what my mum would have said to some random mother ringing her on Christmas morning, asking if their kid could come over to play a video game. I assume she would have reacted in the classic British manner: agreeing to it with bemusement while silently seething, resenting the interloper for every surrendered mince pie.

I joke! I had no friends. I did have Zelda, though. - Ed.

Community "I Think Of Her Every Time I Play It" - Your Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Memories

We seem to have sleepwalked into an era of walking simulators.

I’m not talking about artsy indie games emphasising investigation over action, but big budget AAA titles starring main “characters” who look like they’ve walked out of a Hollywood movie. There are too many humans in games and it’s stifling the medium.

Back when the mascot character was king, protagonists felt properly differentiated both aesthetically and mechanically: Mario jumps, Sonic runs, Spyro flies, Crash bangs and wallops. Of these, only Mario could be called ‘human’, and even he has about as much in common with a real plumber as Sonic does with a real hedgehog.

Vibrant colours and exaggerated movements helped make the games legible on small screens when pixels, polygons and processing power came at a premium, and this gave games a unique vibe and feel. Now that we can better render humans in all their hairy, fleshy complexity, video game aesthetics have moved from ‘cartoonish’ to ‘cinematic’, and physics have followed suit.

Thing is, if I wanted to control a human, I’d put the controller down and go for a walk. (…Maybe not a bad idea actually). We’re meandering, clunky lumps of meat who navigate the world in a most pedestrian manner. Fine for a trip to the shops. Not the most inspiring thing to control in a video game.

It should be said that the ‘mascot character’ isn’t completely dead. The House of Mario was built by pixelated protags who carry the forward the flame of the 8-bit era. The portly purported plumber is still as satisfyingly springy as ever. DK has swapped pixels for vowels but continues to dish out delightful destruction like a primate possessed. Even the new squid-kids on the block - Splatoon’s Inklings - are unashamedly ‘gamey’, slipping slickly through their own mercurial fluids.

It’s a pleasant reminder that video games let us be anything we want: a bird (Untitled Goose Game), a plane (Star Fox) or even a kickflipping train (Denshattack). With that in mind, it seems a shame to be stuck as the same humdrum human that AAA titles insist on lumbering us with.

As film studios conglomerate and cinematic universes bleed into each other, I wish video games would embrace what makes them unique rather than dissolving into the same great multimedia melange. I’ve had enough of the homogeneous Homo sapiens-centric pseudo-cinema now synonymous with AAA game development and wish that more creative energies would be put into games that actually push the mechanical possibilities of the medium.

I disagree, purely because there are just so many games of all flavours out there. If you want to be a squirrel or a crab or an insect or anything else, there's never been a better time. Big, small, there's just so much incredible variety. If AAA isn't doing it for you, the other As have got you covered.

I get the sense perhaps you're reacting to the priority of animation over gamefeel in some cases - lumpy realistic animation versus snappy response? Pushing right on the stick and a moment later a soupy animation cycle transitions into the movement you've input (as opposed to Mario or Link responding instantly, if unrealistically).

If that's the case, I agree that Nintendo's approach is my preference, whatever form of animal, vegetable or mineral you're controlling. The animation of an Assassin's Creed or a GTA is incredibly impressive, but it's interminably slow if you're coming to it with a Mario mindset. I find I have to be invested in the cinema and 'show' of those games if they're going to click. My all-time favourites tend to have much more responsive controls, though. - Ed.

When Nintendo announced Pikmin Day this year for November 1st, it seemed to me that it was met with mixed reactions. People said that saying 11/1 looks like Pikmin is a bit of a stretch, and they didn't really announce anything particularly interesting. While this is true, I found it positively delightful, specifically the second half of the direct when Fuka Koshiba was revealed to be hired by Nintendo. While their conversation was a bit awkward (as Nintendo Direct dialogue always is), I thought it was super cool that they hired her just from seeing her posts on Instagram. And I've been loving the charming shorts that they've been releasing recently. And I'm not even a big Pikmin fan!

The direct was weird, certainly unnecessary, and a bit awkward, but that's what made it amazing. It was delightfully quirky, dumb, delightful, and wholly Nintendo.

I think any rational person will have responded to the 'Pikmin Day' declaration in the same way: wut. Anyone but Nintendo would have been torn to absolute shreds.

Frankly, though, with everything else going on in the world, if Shigsy wants to claim some random day for what might be their best series, crack on. A '1' looks like a Pikmin, you say, Miyamoto-san? Sure, fine. So, Pikmin 5 announcement next November, hmm? - Ed.

"For Pokémon day next year, I want a Pok" - Scottdevine53

That's all for this month! Thanks to everyone who wrote in, whether you were featured above or not.

#3957. Microsoft suffer system outage affecting Outlook, Teams and Copilot, exec says there's "no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity"

Microsoft 365 isn't quite living up to its name this week, as its services have suffered an extended outage that's knocked the likes of Outlook, Teams, and Copilot for six. As of writing, the company are finally reporting "encouraging recovery progress in Europe" and are busy "addressing the remaining areas of disruption", but that's only after chunks of November 12th and 13th have seen people, businesses, and institutions left unable to use stuff they rely on.

That latest update was given by Microsoft to the BBC, who've had a live report on the outage running, since it's affected the likes of schools, government services and medical services. IGN and Kotaku's reports differ on whether any Xbox services appear to be affected. The Xbox status support page currently indicates all is swell, but Downdetector does show a recent uptick in reports of issues.

"We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue," Microsoft exec Charles LaManna wrote in response to a support thread on the topic in the early hours of November 13th UK time. "We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity."

As much as it's slightly reassuring that there currently looks to have been no big hack, the time it's taken to deploy proper fixes is concerning, with Microsoft noting some of their early attempts at rectifying things "not taking as expected".

The debacle has rather emphasised how far from ideal it is that so much key infrastructure across the world runs on one clump of tech which all go down in a heartbeat, but to a certain degree that is the peril of relying on anything. One can only hope that Microsoft's ongoing efforts to fire vast numbers of staff into the sun and embrace AI haven't factored into lots of their services going tits up for an inconvenient amount of time.

#3956. Umamusume: Pretty Derby parent company plans to release seven new games by 2030 as it boasts an "88 percent hit rate" on its mobile titles

Cyberagent - the parent company of Umamusume: Pretty Derby developer Cygames - has boasted its recent successes in the mobile gaming sphere in a recent quarterly earnings presentation.

As part of this presentation (covered by Automaton), the company has established plans to launch seven "major releases" to the mobile platform by 2030. There is no word on what these games will be, but one will be released in 2027, while another two will come in 2028.

Cyberagent boasted an 88 percent "hit" rate for its mobile releases so far, with seven of its eight releases having a development budget of around a billion yen, and reaching a point where it makes that figure back every month from its playerbases. Those games include Umamusume: Pretty Derby, Final Fantasy Ever Crisis, Hololive Dreams, and Jujutsu Kaisen Phantom Parade.

CyberAgent CEO Takahiro Yamauchi - speaking during the presentation - noted that it was still difficult to predict the success of a mobile game ahead of its release. However, he also claims that the experience Cyberagent has gained with its big releases to date have allowed the company to gain a clearer perspective on profitability and sustainability.

This presentation comes after a notable month for Cygmes and Umamusume: Pretty Derby. The developer issued refunds for hotels and flights following the sudden cancellation of an LA live show for the game last month, then shortly after became a major sponsor of the Japanese Formula 1 Grand Prix. The game was also temporarily taken offline due to the major PHP vulnerability exposed last month, an outage that was thankfully short-lived.

#3955. The next Xbox, Project Helix, is a console and "not a PC" says Microsoft, as it clarifies that computational power isn't sole focus this time

"It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering."

Microsoft has stressed that its next-generation Xbox console, Project Helix, "is not a PC that can also play console games", but rather "a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC". The company has also underlined the importance of using gen-AI-adjacent "neural rendering" technology going forwards, and a desire to remove "all the barriers of play that have historically existed" - notably in making the past generations of games playable.

The details come from a Microsoft-produced Xbox magazine made available digitally yesterday, and a Helix-related feature speaking to Xbox vice president of next generation, Jason Ronald. "When we think about Project Helix, it's really designed to be the ultimate gaming machine," Ronald said, "one that removes all the barriers of play that have historically existed. My entire library is accessible to me. I'm able to bring four generations of my Xbox library and progression with me and have it available instantly. And we remove the arbitrary constraints between console and PC games.

"We're very clear on the design goal," Ronald later added. "Helix is designed to be a console that is also capable of playing games from your PC. It is not a PC that can also play console games. The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games. But if you're a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customisability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it."

Notably, Ronald seemed to suggest that Helix - the console, not the handheld; "Helix" refers to a couple of machines - isn't solely focused on computational grunt. Indeed, he said the next generation wasn't about hitting 8K resolutions and 240 hertz frame-rates, but instead leaning on technologies like "neural rendering" - i.e. generative-AI - and encouraging innovation.

"It's about deeper immersion," Ronald said. "It is about leveraging new technical advancements such as neural rendering to deliver a new level of visual fidelity in more efficient and innovative ways. It's about new kinds of games and new game experiences that we haven't been able to do before. What excites me about the future is the idea of entirely new types of games that have never been possible before, delivered through all the innovation in the silicon and the hardware and the platform that we're delivering."

While referencing the global component shortage and exorbitant prices of computer hardware, he added: "This is a big reason why we're really focused on advancements like neural rendering because it's an entirely new way to generate a frame without requiring more computational horsepower, additional memory, and things like that. I think you're going to see more innovation over the next three to five years than you've seen in the last 10 years."

Xbox boss Asha Sharma also recently talked up the importance of generative-AI-sounding technology in Xbox's future, saying "too many ideas never become games", and that "a single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations".

Another key part of Xbox's Helix vision is compatibility and game preservation. "Game preservation is core to Xbox," Ronald went as far as to say. "Not only do we feel like it's the right thing for the industry, we feel a deep responsibility as one of its biggest platforms and publishers. For the first 30 years of game development, nobody really thought about game preservation when they were designing their hardware, when they were building their games." Xbox is apparently working with game-makers to ensure games can not only be played now but also 20 to 30 years into the future.

The other key facet of Microsoft's push the familiar Play Anywhere mantra, whereby one game can be played across multiple devices, maintaining your game-progress as you go. This is fundamental to Microsoft's handheld-and-console Helix plan, and something we've seen the company dry-run with the Xbox ROG Ally X handheld. "It's this notion that not only does my library move with me, but my progress moves with me as well," Ronald said. "Because I fully expect that when I'm in the middle of an 80-hour RPG, if I'm 25 hours into that and I want to play it on another device, I should be able to instantly resume from where I was. Those are things that today are becoming more common, but I think in the future it's going to be a baseline expectation of all players."

Ronald wouldn't be drawn on the issue of price regarding Project Helix - a recent report suggested Helix could be priced up to $1800 - referring to it only as both "a challenging time" but an "exciting one", because "we have to invent entirely new technology to continue to advance the state-of-the-art while also continuing to make things accessible and affordable". Ronald also wouldn't reference a release date, though the report referenced above suggested the handheld Helix machine will release next holiday, 2027, and the console Helix machine the year after. The next generation, then, seems to be around the corner.
